name: shiftwork_clock_out
title: Shift work: clock out
description: Shift-work clock-out: record that a unit finished — set its status, advance plan.cursor, merge `handoff_patch` into handoff, push `history_entry` onto the 5-entry history ring, and append one accounting line to <checkpoint>.log.jsonl. Call it once per unit after its agent returns: shiftwork_clock_in briefs, this tool closes, and shiftwork_status reads what both wrote. The whole mutated document is validated against the checkpoint schema BEFORE one atomic write, so a failure writes nothing and answers {"result": "error", "reason": ...}; nothing is ever deleted from the checkpoint. `unit_id` must be plan.cursor — which needs no brief and clocks out with briefed=false — or a unit clock_in briefed since its own last clock-out; any other id is refused with `unit X is not the cursor unit Y`. `handoff_patch` and `history_entry` are both required arguments: pass `{}` to leave handoff unchanged, and give history_entry at least `unit` and `outcome`. plan.cursor then moves to the head of the ready batch recomputed on the new document — plan.units order over the remaining non-terminal units when the graph cannot batch, `unit_id` when none remain. The accounting line carries unit, role, status, ts and `briefed` (written by the runtime, never taken from you: true only when a brief was issued since this unit's LAST clock-out) plus your `accounting` fields when given. `follow_ups` appends the work it discovered as todo units. `agreements` adopts or retires a working agreement every later brief carries. Each clock-out also appends {status, outcome, notes?, produced?} to the unit's attempts (newest 3 kept). With job.budget declared, a line reporting 0 tokens is refused unless it carries `estimate: true`. When job.roles names this unit's role, `accounting.model` must be on that role's list, spelled exactly, or nothing is written — see the `model` property.

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint
checkpoint.description: Path to the shift-work checkpoint JSON file (by convention .shiftwork/checkpoint.json in the repo the job works on), absolute or relative to the server's working directory. The same file shiftwork_plan, shiftwork_clock_in and shiftwork_clock_out take; it must validate against assets/schemas/shiftwork-checkpoint.json.

unit_id.title: Unit Id
unit_id.description: The unit being clocked out. Must be plan.cursor, or a unit briefed since its own last clock-out: clock_in briefs the cursor unit by default and, when its unit_id names one, any unit shiftwork_plan reports in `ready` — and that brief is what lets clock_out accept a unit the cursor is not on.

status.title: Status
status.description: The unit's new status; the same five values the checkpoint schema allows on plan.units[].status.

handoff_patch.title: Handoff Patch
handoff_patch.description: Shallow-merged into `handoff`: only these four keys exist there, and a key outside them is refused by the schema check. Required; `{}` leaves `handoff` unchanged.

anyOf.description: A decision question: the user's to answer.

kind.description: `decision` needs the user; `relay` is answered by its probe.

probe.description: Shell command run from the repo root by clock_in; exit 0 answers the relay. Required on a relay, or nothing is written.

open_questions.description: The autonomy switch: empty = driver keeps cycling, non-empty = STOP and ask. A bare string is a decision; a `relay` question carries a `probe` that clock_in runs instead of escalating (#225).

do_not.description: Negative space — near-mistakes past sessions made.

notes.description: Free-form prose for the next session, one string; the empty string clears it.

history_entry.title: History Entry
history_entry.description: Pushed onto the 5-entry `history` ring; `unit` and `outcome` are required, `notes` optional, other keys pass through.

unit.description: The unit this entry is about — normally the `unit_id` being clocked out.

outcome.description: What happened, in a few words: done, blocked on X, dropped because Y.

notes.description: Optional free text for the next session reading the ring, and recorded in the unit's attempt (#259): at most 2000 code points.

kind.description: What sort of thing: commit, file, pr, run-output.

ref.description: Where it is: a SHA, a path, a URL.

produced.description: What the unit produced, [{kind, ref}] (a commit, a file, a run output). Recorded with the unit's attempt, and handed to every unit that depends on it as upstream[].last.

anyOf.description: Per-unit cost. Written verbatim, beside ts/unit/role/status, as one line of <checkpoint>.log.jsonl - the ledger the N-sessions experiment reads. The keys named here have fixed meanings so a reader holding only the ledger knows what each number counts, in which unit, and which model produced it; any other key passes through unchanged, except the six the runtime writes itself — unit, role, status, ts, event, agent_id — which are refused (result=error) before anything is written; a self-reported briefed is overwritten, not refused. Lines written before this schema existed may spell these differently; the schema governs new writes only.

tokens.description: Tokens the unit consumed as the harness's subagent counter reports them: every class it reports (input, output, cache creation) summed, EXCLUDING cache reads. In a non-null accounting line it is required — a line without it is refused before anything is written; only `accounting: null`, the default, is exempt, and that logs no cost at all. A rounded self-estimate is allowed only if `note` says it is one; a unit whose cost is unknown cannot be compared with any other.

cache_read_tokens.description: Tokens the unit's requests served from prompt cache, kept OUT of `tokens` because they dominate a real session's traffic and would swamp the work signal. Optional: omit it when the harness reports no such figure - a written 0 means the unit read nothing from cache.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock from spawning the subagent to its final message, in whole milliseconds. In a non-null line it is required, and it is the only duration key with a defined meaning: older lines carry `duration`, `duration_min` or `duration_s`, which this schema neither reads nor renames.

model.description: The exact identifier of the model the subagent actually ran on (e.g. `claude-sonnet-5`) and nothing else - a caveat about how it was chosen belongs in `note`. Not required here: when the checkpoint's job.roles names this unit's role, clock_out already requires it and refuses a value off that role's list, spelled exactly; a checkpoint with no job.roles leaves it optional. This schema does not change that gate.

tool_uses.description: Tool calls the subagent made, as the harness counts them. Optional; it is the denominator that makes `tokens` comparable across units of different size (per-unit cost is linear in tool calls, not in unit length).

estimate.description: true when `tokens` is a guess rather than the host's figure. With job.budget declared, a line reporting 0 tokens is refused unless it carries estimate: true.

note.description: Free text for what the fields above cannot say: that `tokens` is an estimate, that this is a retry or a second scope under the same unit id, what a harness counter excludes. Anything that is not a model identifier goes here, not in `model`.

accounting.title: Accounting
accounting.description: Per-unit cost line, or null (the default) to log a line with no cost figures at all. A non-null line must carry `tokens` and `duration_ms`; `model` is required when job.roles names this unit's role. The object shape is described below.

id.description: The new unit's id; must not be a unit already, nor repeat in this list.

role.description: Who runs it; when job.roles is declared it must be one of its keys.

brief_path.description: Its brief, a file that must already exist, relative to the repo (the nearest ancestor of the checkpoint holding .git).

depends_on.description: Unit ids it waits for; absent means the unit being clocked out.

verify.description: Command proving it done; absent means the clocked-out unit's verify.

follow_ups.title: Follow Ups
follow_ups.description: Work this unit discovered (#260): each item becomes a todo unit appended to plan.units in the given order, on the same write. Refused whole, nothing written, on a duplicate id, a brief that is not a file, an unknown dependency or a cycle (the planner's sentence), or a role job.roles does not declare.

adopt.description: Agreements to add to job.agreements; text already listed is left as it is.

retire.description: Agreements to remove, by exact text; one not on the list is refused.

agreements.title: Agreements
agreements.description: A lesson this unit wants every later brief to carry (#261): retire by exact text, then adopt. Refused, nothing written, for text not on the list or a result over 20; each applied change is recorded in retro[].

outcome.description: `inconclusive` and `stopped` are never refused; `resolved` needs the evidence below.

supported.description: The hypothesis id the evidence supports; required for `resolved`.

evidence.description: Refs to what was observed: run outputs, commits, files.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.description: An investigation's answer (#264), written to job.conclusion. Only a unit with `concludes: true` may send it; `resolved` is refused unless `supported` has a done run, a done replay of that run in another role, and a done review of either. A run unit (`tests` or `replay_of`) clocked out done must report a `run-output` in history_entry.produced.

agent_id.title: Agent Id
agent_id.description: The `agentId` the Agent tool's result returned for this unit's subagent (#266), copied verbatim: 1 to 64 letters, digits, - or _, or nothing is written. It goes on the accounting line, never into the checkpoint, and is how the skill miner attributes the skill uses the hook logged inside that subagent to this unit. Omit it for a unit run inline.

result.description: `ok` when the checkpoint was rewritten; `error` with `reason` when the call was refused and nothing was written.

log.description: Path of the <checkpoint>.log.jsonl the accounting line was appended to.

reason.description: With result `error`: one sentence saying why the call was refused.
